name: Phaser.Animations.Animation
doc: A Frame based Animation. Animations in Phaser consist of a sequence of `AnimationFrame` objects, which are managed by this class, along with properties that impact playback, such as the animation's frame rate or delay.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.constructor
sig: constructor(manager: Phaser.Animations.AnimationManager, key: string, config: Phaser.Types.Animations.Animation)

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.manager
doc: A reference to the global Animation Manager.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.key
doc: The unique identifying string for this animation.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.type
doc: A frame-based animation (as opposed to a bone-based animation).

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.frames
doc: An array of AnimationFrame objects that make up this animation.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.frameRate
doc: The frame rate of playback in frames per second (default 24 if duration is null)

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.duration
doc: How long the animation should play for, in milliseconds. If the `frameRate` property has been set then it overrides this value, otherwise the `frameRate` is derived from `duration`.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.msPerFrame
doc: How many ms per frame, not including frame-specific modifiers.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.skipMissedFrames
doc: Skip frames if the time lags, or always advance anyway?

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.delay
doc: The delay in ms before the playback will begin.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.repeat
doc: Number of times to repeat the animation. Set to -1 to repeat forever.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.repeatDelay
doc: The delay in ms before a repeat play starts.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.yoyo
doc: Should the animation yoyo (reverse back down to the start) before repeating?

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.showBeforeDelay
doc: If the animation has a delay set, before playback will begin, this controls when the first frame is set on the Sprite. If this property is 'false' then the frame is set only after the delay has expired.

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.showOnStart
doc: Should the GameObject's `visible` property be set to `true` when the animation starts to play?

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.hideOnComplete
doc: Should the GameObject's `visible` property be set to `false` when the animation finishes?

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.randomFrame
doc: Start playback of this animation from a random frame?

name: Phaser.Animations.Animation.paused
doc: Global pause. All Game Objects using this Animation instance are impacted by this property.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState
doc: The Animation State Component. This component provides features to apply animations to Game Objects.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.constructor
doc: @param parent The Game Object to which this animation component belongs.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.parent
doc: The Game Object to which this animation component belongs. You can typically access this component from the Game Object via the `this.anims` property.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.animationManager
doc: A reference to the global Animation Manager.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.textureManager
doc: A reference to the Texture Manager.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.anims
doc: The Animations stored locally in this Animation component. Do not modify the contents of this Map directly, instead use the `add`, `create` and `remove` methods of this class instead.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.isPlaying
doc: Is an animation currently playing or not?

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.hasStarted
doc: Has the current animation started playing, or is it waiting for a delay to expire?

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.currentAnim
doc: The current Animation loaded into this Animation component. Will be `null` if no animation is yet loaded.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.currentFrame
doc: The current AnimationFrame being displayed by this Animation component. Will be `null` if no animation is yet loaded.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.nextAnim
doc: The key, instance, or config of the next Animation to be loaded into this Animation component when the current animation completes. Will be `null` if no animation has been queued.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.nextAnimsQueue
doc: A queue of Animations to be loaded into this Animation component when the current animation completes. Populate this queue via the `chain` method.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.timeScale
doc: The Time Scale factor. You can adjust this value to modify the passage of time for the animation that is currently playing.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.frameRate
doc: The frame rate of playback, of the current animation, in frames per second. This value is set when a new animation is loaded into this component and should be treated as read-only, as changing it once playback has started will not alter the animation.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.duration
doc: The duration of the current animation, in milliseconds. This value is set when a new animation is loaded into this component and should be treated as read-only, as changing it once playback has started will not alter the animation.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.msPerFrame
doc: The number of milliseconds per frame, not including frame specific modifiers that may be present in the Animation data. This value is calculated when a new animation is loaded into this component and should be treated as read-only.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.skipMissedFrames
doc: Skip frames if the time lags, or always advanced anyway?

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.randomFrame
doc: Start playback of this animation from a random frame?

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.delay
doc: The delay before starting playback of the current animation, in milliseconds. This value is set when a new animation is loaded into this component and should be treated as read-only, as changing it once playback has started will not alter the animation.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.repeat
doc: The number of times to repeat playback of the current animation. If -1, it means the animation will repeat forever.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.repeatDelay
doc: The number of milliseconds to wait before starting the repeat playback of the current animation. This value is set when a new animation is loaded into this component, but can also be modified at run-time.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.yoyo
doc: Should the current animation yoyo? An animation that yoyos will play in reverse, from the end to the start, before then repeating or completing. An animation that does not yoyo will just play from the start to the end.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.showBeforeDelay
doc: If the animation has a delay set, before playback will begin, this controls when the first frame is set on the Sprite. If this property is 'false' then the frame is set only after the delay has expired.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.showOnStart
doc: Should the GameObject's `visible` property be set to `true` when the animation starts to play? This will happen _after_ any delay that may have been set. This value is set when a new animation is loaded into this component, but can also be modified at run-time, assuming the animation is currently delayed.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.hideOnComplete
doc: Should the GameObject's `visible` property be set to `false` when the animation completes? This value is set when a new animation is loaded into this component, but can also be modified at run-time, assuming the animation is still actively playing.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.forward
doc: Is the playhead moving forwards (`true`) or in reverse (`false`) ?

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.inReverse
doc: An internal trigger that tells the component if it should plays the animation in reverse mode ('true') or not ('false'). This is used because `forward` can be changed by the `yoyo` feature.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.accumulator
doc: Internal time overflow accumulator. This has the `delta` time added to it as part of the `update` step.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.nextTick
doc: The time point at which the next animation frame will change. This value is compared against the `accumulator` as part of the `update` step.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.delayCounter
doc: A counter keeping track of how much delay time, in milliseconds, is left before playback begins. This is set via the `playAfterDelay` method, although it can be modified at run-time if required, as long as the animation has not already started playing.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.repeatCounter
doc: A counter that keeps track of how many repeats are left to run. This value is set when a new animation is loaded into this component, but can also be modified at run-time.

name: Phaser.Animations.AnimationState.pendingRepeat
doc: An internal flag keeping track of pending repeats.

doc: A Base Camera class. The Camera is the way in which all games are rendered in Phaser.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.constructor
sig: constructor(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number)

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.scene
doc: A reference to the Scene this camera belongs to.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.sceneManager
doc: A reference to the Game Scene Manager.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.scaleManager
doc: A reference to the Game Scale Manager.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.cameraManager
doc: A reference to the Scene's Camera Manager to which this Camera belongs.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.id
doc: The Camera ID. Assigned by the Camera Manager and used to handle camera exclusion.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.name
doc: The name of the Camera. This is left empty for your own use.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.roundPixels
doc: Should this camera round its pixel values to integers?

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.visible
doc: Is this Camera visible or not? A visible camera will render and perform input tests. An invisible camera will not render anything and will skip input tests.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.useBounds
doc: Is this Camera using a bounds to restrict scrolling movement? Set this property along with the bounds via `Camera.setBounds`.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.worldView
doc: The World View is a Rectangle that defines the area of the 'world' the Camera is currently looking at. This factors in the Camera viewport size, zoom and scroll position and is updated in the Camera preRender step.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.dirty
doc: Is this Camera dirty? A dirty Camera has had either its viewport size, bounds, scroll, rotation or zoom levels changed since the last frame. This flag is cleared during rendering with the new values.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.matrixCombined
doc: A local transform matrix combining `matrix` and `matrixExternal`.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.matrixExternal
doc: A local transform matrix used to compute the camera location.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.transparent
doc: Does this Camera have a transparent background?

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.backgroundColor
doc: The background color of this Camera. Only used if `transparent` is `false`.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.alpha
doc: The Camera alpha value. Setting this property impacts every single object that this Camera renders.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.disableCull
doc: Should the camera cull Game Objects before checking them for input hit tests? In some special cases it may be beneficial to disable this.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.midPoint
doc: The mid-point of the Camera in 'world' coordinates. Use it to obtain exactly where in the world the center of the camera is currently looking.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.originX
doc: The horizontal origin of rotation for this Camera. By default the camera rotates around the center of the viewport.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.originY
doc: The vertical origin of rotation for this Camera. By default the camera rotates around the center of the viewport.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.mask
doc: The Mask this Camera is using during render. Set the mask using the `setMask` method.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.renderList
doc: This array is populated with all of the Game Objects that this Camera has rendered in the previous (or current, depending on when you inspect it) frame. It is cleared at the start of `Camera.preUpdate`, or if the Camera is destroyed.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.isSceneCamera
doc: Is this Camera a Scene Camera? (which is the default), or a Camera belonging to a Texture?

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.forceComposite
doc: Whether to force the camera to render via a framebuffer. This only applies when using the WebGL renderer.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.renderRoundPixels
doc: Can this Camera render rounded pixel values? This property is updated during the `preRender` method and should not be set directly. It is set based on the `roundPixels` property of the Camera combined with the zoom level.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Scene2D.BaseCamera.addToRenderList

Adds the given Game Object to this camera's render list. This is invoked during the rendering stage.
@param child The Game Object to add to the render list.

@returns This Key Control instance.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.FixedKeyControl.stop
doc:
Stops this Key Control from running. Call `start` to start it again.undefined
@returns This Key Control instance.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.FixedKeyControl.setCamera
Phaser.Cameras.Controls.FixedKeyControl.update
doc:
Applies the results of pressing the control keys to the Camera. You must call this every step, it is not called automatically.
@param delta The delta time in ms since the last frame. This is a smoothed and capped value based on the FPS rate.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.FixedKeyControl.destroy
doc: Destroys this Key Control, nulling its camera and key references to allow for garbage collection. This Key Control cannot be used again after being destroyed.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl
doc: A Smoothed Key Camera Control. This allows you to control the movement and zoom of a camera using the defined keys.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.constructor
doc: @param config The Smoothed Key Control configuration object.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.camera
doc: The Camera that this Control will update.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.left
doc: The Key to be pressed that will move the Camera left.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.right
doc: The Key to be pressed that will move the Camera right.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.up
doc: The Key to be pressed that will move the Camera up.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.down
doc: The Key to be pressed that will move the Camera down.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.zoomIn
doc: The Key to be pressed that will zoom the Camera in.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.zoomOut
doc: The Key to be pressed that will zoom the Camera out.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.zoomSpeed
doc: The speed at which the camera will zoom if the `zoomIn` or `zoomOut` keys are pressed.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.minZoom
doc: The smallest zoom value the camera will reach when zoomed out.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.maxZoom
doc: The largest zoom value the camera will reach when zoomed in.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.accelX
doc: The horizontal acceleration applied to the camera's movement when a directional key is held down.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.accelY
doc: The vertical acceleration applied to the camera's movement when a directional key is held down.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.dragX
doc: The horizontal drag applied to the camera when it is moving.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.dragY
doc: The vertical drag applied to the camera when it is moving.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.maxSpeedX
doc: The maximum horizontal speed the camera can reach.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.maxSpeedY
doc: The maximum vertical speed the camera can reach.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.active
doc: A flag controlling if the Controls will update the Camera or not.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.start
doc:
Starts the Key Control running, providing it has been linked to a camera.undefined
@returns This Key Control instance.

name: Phaser.Cameras.Controls.SmoothedKeyControl.stop
doc:
Stops this Key Control from running. Call `start` to start it again.undefined
@returns This Key Control instance.

Applies the results of pressing the control keys to the Camera. You must call this every step, it is not called automatically.

name: Phaser.Game
doc: The Phaser.Game instance is the main controller for the entire Phaser game. It is responsible for handling the boot process, parsing the configuration values, creating the renderer, and setting-up all of the global Phaser systems, such as sound and input.

name: Phaser.Game.constructor
doc: @param config The configuration object for your Phaser Game instance.

name: Phaser.Game.config
doc: The parsed Game Configuration object. The values stored within this object are read-only and should not be changed at run-time.

name: Phaser.Game.domContainer
doc: A reference to an HTML Div Element used as the DOM Element Container. Only set if `createDOMContainer` is `true` in the game config (by default it is `false`) and if you provide a parent element to insert the Phaser Game inside.

name: Phaser.Game.canvas
doc: A reference to the HTML Canvas Element that Phaser uses to render the game. This is created automatically by Phaser unless you provide a `canvas` property in your Game Config.

name: Phaser.Game.context
doc: A reference to the Rendering Context belonging to the Canvas Element this game is rendering to. If the game is running under Canvas it will be a 2d Canvas Rendering Context.

name: Phaser.Game.isBooted
doc: A flag indicating when this Game instance has finished its boot process.

name: Phaser.Game.isRunning
doc: A flag indicating if this Game is currently running its game step or not.

name: Phaser.Game.events
doc: An Event Emitter which is used to broadcast game-level events from the global systems.

name: Phaser.Game.anims
doc: An instance of the Animation Manager. The Animation Manager is a global system responsible for managing all animations used within your game.

name: Phaser.Game.textures
doc: An instance of the Texture Manager. The Texture Manager is a global system responsible for managing all textures being used by your game.

name: Phaser.Game.cache
doc: An instance of the Cache Manager. The Cache Manager is a global system responsible for caching, accessing and releasing external game assets.

name: Phaser.Game.registry
doc: An instance of the Data Manager. This is a global manager, available from any Scene and allows you to share and exchange your own game-level data or events without having to use an internal event system.

name: Phaser.Game.input
doc: An instance of the Input Manager. The Input Manager is a global system responsible for the capture of browser-level input events.

name: Phaser.Game.scene
doc: An instance of the Scene Manager. The Scene Manager is a global system responsible for creating, modifying and updating the Scenes in your game.

name: Phaser.Game.device
doc: A reference to the Device inspector. Contains information about the device running this game, such as OS, browser vendor and feature support.

name: Phaser.Game.scale
doc: An instance of the Scale Manager. The Scale Manager is a global system responsible for handling scaling of the game canvas.

name: Phaser.Game.loop
doc: An instance of the Time Step. The Time Step is a global system responsible for setting-up and responding to the browser frame events, processing them and calculating delta values.

name: Phaser.Game.plugins
doc: An instance of the Plugin Manager. The Plugin Manager is a global system that allows plugins to register themselves with it, and can then install those plugins into Scenes as required.

name: Phaser.Game.hasFocus
doc: Does the window the game is running in currently have focus or not? This is modified by the VisibilityHandler.

name: Phaser.Game.isPaused
doc: Is the Game currently paused? This will stop everything from updating, except the `TimeStep` and related RequestAnimationFrame or setTimeout. Those will continue stepping, but the core Game step will be skipped.

name: Phaser.Game.boot
doc: This method is called automatically when the DOM is ready. It is responsible for creating the renderer, displaying the Debug Header, adding the game canvas to the DOM and emitting the 'boot' event.

name: Phaser.Game.start
doc: Called automatically by Game.boot once all of the global systems have finished setting themselves up. By this point the Game is now ready to start the main loop running.

name: Phaser.Game.step
Phaser.Game.headlessStep
Phaser.Game.onHidden
doc: Called automatically by the Visibility Handler. This will pause the main loop and then emit a pause event.

name: Phaser.Game.pause
doc: This will pause the entire game and emit a `PAUSE` event. All of Phaser's internal systems will be paused and the game will not re-render.

name: Phaser.Game.onVisible
doc: Called automatically by the Visibility Handler. This will resume the main loop and then emit a resume event.

name: Phaser.Game.resume
doc: This will resume the entire game and emit a `RESUME` event. All of Phaser's internal systems will be resumed and the game will start rendering again.

name: Phaser.Game.onBlur
doc: Called automatically by the Visibility Handler. This will set the main loop into a 'blurred' state, which pauses it.

name: Phaser.Game.onFocus
doc: Called automatically by the Visibility Handler. This will set the main loop into a 'focused' state, which resumes it.

name: Phaser.Game.getFrame
doc:
Returns the current game frame. When the game starts running, the frame is incremented every time Request Animation Frame, or Set Timeout, fires.undefined
@returns The current game frame.

name: Phaser.Game.getTime
doc:
Returns the time that the current game step started at, as based on `performance.now`.undefined
@returns The current game timestamp.

name: Phaser.Game.destroy
Phaser.Core.Config
doc: The active game configuration settings, parsed from a {@link Phaser.Types.Core.GameConfig} object. This class takes the raw configuration object passed to `new Phaser.Game()` and resolves all values, applying defaults where properties are not specified.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.constructor
doc: @param GameConfig The configuration object for your Phaser Game instance.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.width
doc: The width of the underlying canvas, in pixels.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.height
doc: The height of the underlying canvas, in pixels.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.zoom
doc: The zoom factor, as used by the Scale Manager.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.parent
doc: A parent DOM element into which the canvas created by the renderer will be injected.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.scaleMode
doc: The scale mode as used by the Scale Manager. The default is zero, which is no scaling.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.expandParent
doc: Is the Scale Manager allowed to adjust the CSS height property of the parent to be 100%?

name: Phaser.Core.Config.autoRound
doc: Automatically round the display and style sizes of the canvas. This can help with performance in lower-powered devices.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.autoCenter
doc: Automatically center the canvas within the parent?

name: Phaser.Core.Config.resizeInterval
doc: How many ms should elapse before checking if the browser size has changed?

name: Phaser.Core.Config.fullscreenTarget
doc: The DOM element that will be sent into full screen mode, or its `id`. If undefined Phaser will create its own div and insert the canvas into it when entering fullscreen mode.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.minWidth
doc: The minimum width, in pixels, the canvas will scale down to. A value of zero means no minimum.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.maxWidth
doc: The maximum width, in pixels, the canvas will scale up to. A value of zero means no maximum.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.minHeight
doc: The minimum height, in pixels, the canvas will scale down to. A value of zero means no minimum.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.maxHeight
doc: The maximum height, in pixels, the canvas will scale up to. A value of zero means no maximum.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.snapWidth
doc: The horizontal amount to snap the canvas by when the Scale Manager is resizing. A value of zero means no snapping.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.snapHeight
doc: The vertical amount to snap the canvas by when the Scale Manager is resizing. A value of zero means no snapping.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.renderType
doc: Force Phaser to use a specific renderer. Can be `CONST.CANVAS`, `CONST.WEBGL`, `CONST.HEADLESS` or `CONST.AUTO` (default)

name: Phaser.Core.Config.canvas
doc: Force Phaser to use your own Canvas element instead of creating one.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.context
doc: Force Phaser to use your own Canvas context instead of creating one.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.canvasStyle
doc: Optional CSS attributes to be set on the canvas object created by the renderer.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.customEnvironment
doc: Is Phaser running under a custom (non-native web) environment? If so, set this to `true` to skip internal Feature detection. If `true` the `renderType` cannot be left as `AUTO`.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.sceneConfig
doc: The default Scene configuration object.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.seed
doc: A seed which the Random Data Generator will use. If not given, a dynamic seed based on the time is used.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.gameTitle
doc: The title of the game.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.gameURL
doc: The URL of the game.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.gameVersion
doc: The version of the game.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.autoFocus
doc: If `true` the window will automatically be given focus immediately and on any future mousedown event.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.stableSort
doc: `false` or `0` = Use the built-in StableSort (needed for older browsers), `true` or `1` = Rely on ES2019 Array.sort being stable (modern browsers only), or `-1` = Try and determine this automatically based on browser inspection (not guaranteed to work, errs on side of caution).

name: Phaser.Core.Config.domCreateContainer
doc: Should the game create a div element to act as a DOM Container? Only enable if you're using DOM Element objects. You must provide a parent object if you use this feature.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.domPointerEvents
doc: The default `pointerEvents` attribute set on the DOM Container.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputKeyboard
doc: Enable the Keyboard Plugin. This can be disabled in games that don't need keyboard input.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputKeyboardEventTarget
doc: The DOM Target to listen for keyboard events on. Defaults to `window` if not specified.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputKeyboardCapture
doc: `preventDefault` will be called on every non-modified key which has a key code in this array. By default, it is empty.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputMouse
doc: Enable the Mouse Plugin. This can be disabled in games that don't need mouse input.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputMouseEventTarget
doc: The DOM Target to listen for mouse events on. Defaults to the game canvas if not specified.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputMousePreventDefaultDown
doc: Should `mousedown` DOM events have `preventDefault` called on them?

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputMousePreventDefaultUp
doc: Should `mouseup` DOM events have `preventDefault` called on them?

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputMousePreventDefaultMove
doc: Should `mousemove` DOM events have `preventDefault` called on them?

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputMousePreventDefaultWheel
doc: Should `wheel` DOM events have `preventDefault` called on them?

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputTouch
doc: Enable the Touch Plugin. This can be disabled in games that don't need touch input.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputTouchEventTarget
doc: The DOM Target to listen for touch events on. Defaults to the game canvas if not specified.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputTouchCapture
doc: Should touch events be captured? I.e. have prevent default called on them.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputActivePointers
doc: The number of Pointer objects created by default. In a mouse-only, or non-multi touch game, you can leave this as 1.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputSmoothFactor
doc: The smoothing factor to apply during Pointer movement. See {@link Phaser.Input.Pointer#smoothFactor}.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputWindowEvents
doc: Should Phaser listen for input events on the Window? If you disable this, events like 'POINTER_UP_OUTSIDE' will no longer fire.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputGamepad
doc: Enable the Gamepad Plugin. This can be disabled in games that don't need gamepad input.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.inputGamepadEventTarget
doc: The DOM Target to listen for gamepad events on. Defaults to `window` if not specified.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.disableContextMenu
doc: Set to `true` to disable the right-click context menu.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.audio
doc: The Audio Configuration object.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.hideBanner
doc: Don't write the banner line to the console.log. See `Phaser.Types.Core.BannerConfig` for details of this object.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.hidePhaser
doc: Omit Phaser's name and version from the banner.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.bannerTextColor
doc: The color of the banner text.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.bannerBackgroundColor
doc: The background colors of the banner.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.fps
doc: The Frame Rate Configuration object, as parsed by the Timestep class.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.autoMobileTextures
doc: If iOS or Android detected, automatically restrict WebGL to use 1 texture per batch. This can help performance on some devices.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.antialias
doc: When set to `true`, WebGL uses linear interpolation to draw scaled or rotated textures, giving a smooth appearance. When set to `false`, WebGL uses nearest-neighbor interpolation, giving a crisper appearance.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.antialiasGL
doc: Sets the `antialias` property when the WebGL context is created. Setting this value does not impact any subsequent textures that are created, or the canvas style attributes.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.mipmapFilter
doc: Sets the mipmap magFilter to be used when creating WebGL textures. Don't set unless you wish to create mipmaps.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.mipmapRegeneration
doc: - Whether to regenerate mipmaps for framebuffers. If this is false, framebuffers will not use mipmaps.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.desynchronized
doc: When set to `true` it will create a desynchronized context for both 2D and WebGL. See https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2019/05/desynchronized for details.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.roundPixels
doc: Draw texture-based Game Objects at only whole-integer positions. Game Objects without textures, like Graphics, ignore this property.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.selfShadow
doc: On textured objects with lighting, this enables self-shadowing based on the diffuse map.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.pathDetailThreshold
doc: Threshold for combining points into a single path in the WebGL renderer for Graphics objects. This can be overridden at the Graphics object level.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.pixelArt
doc: Prevent pixel art from becoming blurred when scaled. It will remain crisp (tells the WebGL renderer to automatically create textures using a nearest-neighbor filter mode).

name: Phaser.Core.Config.smoothPixelArt
doc: WebGL only. Sets `antialias` to true and `pixelArt` to false.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.transparent
doc: Whether the game canvas will have a transparent background.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.alphaStrategy
doc: The default alpha strategy to use when rendering transparent objects with compatible shaders. Strategies other than `keep` will discard fragments instead of turning them transparent, which creates a very grainy look.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.stencil
doc: Whether to enable stencil testing. Disabling this will prevent creation of stencil buffers, which can save framebuffer memory.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.stencilAlphaStrategy
doc: The default alpha strategy to use when rendering stencils. Keeping transparent pixels still creates opaque stencil, which is usually not what you want.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.clearBeforeRender
doc: Whether the game canvas will be cleared between each rendering frame. You can disable this if you have a full-screen background image or game object.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.preserveDrawingBuffer
doc: If the value is true the WebGL buffers will not be cleared and will preserve their values until cleared or overwritten by the author.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.premultipliedAlpha
doc: In WebGL mode, sets the drawing buffer to contain colors with pre-multiplied alpha.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat
doc: Let the browser abort creating a WebGL context if it judges performance would be unacceptable.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.powerPreference
doc: "high-performance", "low-power" or "default". A hint to the browser on how much device power the game might use.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.batchSize
doc: The default WebGL Batch size. Represents the number of _quads_ that can be added to a single batch.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.maxTextures
doc: When in WebGL mode, this sets the maximum number of GPU Textures to use. The default, -1, will use all available units.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.maxLights
doc: The maximum number of lights allowed to be visible within range of a single Camera in the LightManager.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.renderNodes
doc: A map of custom Render Nodes to be added to the WebGL Renderer. The values will be added to the RenderNodeManager, using the keys as the names.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.backgroundColor
doc: The background color of the game canvas. The default is black.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.preBoot
doc: Called before Phaser boots. Useful for initializing anything not related to Phaser that Phaser may require while booting.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.postBoot
doc: A function to run at the end of the boot sequence. At this point, all the game systems have started and plugins have been loaded.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.physics
doc: The Physics Configuration object.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.defaultPhysicsSystem
doc: The default physics system. It will be started for each scene.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.glowQuality
doc: The quality of the Glow filter (defaults to 10)

name: Phaser.Core.Config.glowDistance
doc: The distance of the Glow filter (defaults to 10)

name: Phaser.Core.Config.installGlobalPlugins
doc: An array of global plugins to be installed.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.installScenePlugins
doc: An array of Scene level plugins to be installed.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.defaultPlugins
doc: The plugins installed into every Scene (in addition to CoreScene and Global).

name: Phaser.Core.Config.defaultImage
doc: A base64 encoded PNG that will be used as the default blank texture.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.missingImage
doc: A base64 encoded PNG that will be used as the default texture when a texture is assigned that is missing or not loaded.

name: Phaser.Core.Config.whiteImage
doc: A base64 encoded PNG used as the default solid white texture. This small 4x4 white image is used internally by Phaser for colored Game Objects and tinting.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep
doc: The core runner class that Phaser uses to handle the game loop. It can use either Request Animation Frame, or SetTimeout, based on browser support and config settings, to create a continuous loop within the browser.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.constructor
doc:
@param game A reference to the Phaser.Game instance that owns this Time Step.
@param config The FPS configuration object, as parsed by the Game Config.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.game
doc: A reference to the Phaser.Game instance.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.raf
doc: The Request Animation Frame DOM Event handler.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.started
doc: A flag that is set once the TimeStep has started running and toggled when it stops.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.running
doc: A flag that is set once the TimeStep has started running and toggled when it stops. The difference between this value and `started` is that `running` is toggled when the TimeStep is sent to sleep, where-as `started` remains `true`, only changing if the TimeStep is actually stopped, not just paused.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.minFps
doc: The minimum fps rate you want the Time Step to run at. Setting this cannot guarantee the browser runs at this rate, it merely influences the internal timing values to help the Timestep know when it has gone out of sync.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.targetFps
doc: The target fps rate for the Time Step to run at. Setting this value will not actually change the speed at which the browser runs, that is beyond the control of Phaser.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.fpsLimit
doc: Enforce a frame rate limit. This forces how often the Game step will run.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.hasFpsLimit
doc: Is the FPS rate limited? This is set by setting the Game Config `limit` value to a value above zero. Consider this property as read-only.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.actualFps
doc: An exponential moving average of the frames per second.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.nextFpsUpdate
doc: The time at which the next fps rate update will take place. When an fps update happens, the `framesThisSecond` value is reset.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.framesThisSecond
doc: The number of frames processed this second.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.callback
doc: A callback to be invoked each time the TimeStep steps.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.forceSetTimeOut
doc: You can force the TimeStep to use SetTimeOut instead of Request Animation Frame by setting the `forceSetTimeOut` property to `true` in the Game Configuration object. It cannot be changed at run-time.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.time
doc: The time, updated each step by adding the elapsed delta time to the previous value. This differs from the `TimeStep.now` value, which is the high resolution time value as provided by Request Animation Frame.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.startTime
doc: The time at which the game started running. This value is adjusted if the game is then paused and resumes.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.lastTime
doc: The time of the previous step. This is typically a high resolution timer value, as provided by Request Animation Frame.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.frame
doc: The current frame the game is on. This counter is incremented once every game step, regardless of how much time has passed and is unaffected by delta smoothing.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.inFocus
doc: Is the browser currently considered in focus by the Page Visibility API? This value is set in the `blur` method, which is called automatically by the Game instance.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.pauseDuration
doc: The duration of the most recent game pause, if any, in ms.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.delta
doc: The delta time, in ms, since the last game step. This is a clamped and smoothed average value.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.deltaIndex
doc: Internal index of the delta history position.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.deltaHistory
doc: Internal array holding the previous delta values, used for delta smoothing.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.deltaSmoothingMax
doc: The maximum number of delta values that are retained in order to calculate a smoothed moving average. This can be changed in the Game Config via the `fps.deltaHistory` property.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.panicMax
doc: The number of frames that the cooldown is set to after the browser panics over the FPS rate, usually as a result of switching tabs and regaining focus. This can be changed in the Game Config via the `fps.panicMax` property.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.rawDelta
doc: The actual elapsed time in ms between one update and the next. Unlike with `delta`, no smoothing, capping, or averaging is applied to this value.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.now
doc: The time, set at the start of the current step. This is typically a high resolution timer value, as provided by Request Animation Frame.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.smoothStep
doc: Apply smoothing to the delta value used within Phaser's internal calculations? This can be changed in the Game Config via the `fps.smoothStep` property. The default is `true`.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.blur
doc: Called by the Game instance when the DOM window.onBlur event triggers.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.focus
doc: Called by the Game instance when the DOM window.onFocus event triggers.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.pause
doc: Called when the visibility API says the game is 'hidden' (tab switch out of view, etc)

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.resume
doc: Called when the visibility API says the game is 'visible' again (tab switch back into view, etc)

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.resetDelta
doc: Resets the time, lastTime, fps averages and delta history. Called automatically when a browser sleeps then resumes.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.start
doc:
Starts the Time Step running, if it is not already doing so. Called automatically by the Game Boot process.
@param callback The callback to be invoked each time the Time Step steps.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.smoothDelta
Phaser.Core.TimeStep.updateFPS
doc:
Update the estimate of the frame rate, `fps`. Every second, the number of frames that occurred in that second are included in an exponential moving average of all frames per second, with an alpha of 0.25.
@param time The timestamp passed in from RequestAnimationFrame or setTimeout.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.stepLimitFPS
doc:
The main step method with an fps limiter. This is called each time the browser updates, either by Request Animation Frame, or by Set Timeout.
@param time The timestamp passed in from RequestAnimationFrame or setTimeout.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.step
doc:
The main step method. This is called each time the browser updates, either by Request Animation Frame, or by Set Timeout.
@param time The timestamp passed in from RequestAnimationFrame or setTimeout.

name: Phaser.Core.TimeStep.tick
doc: Manually advances the TimeStep by one step, using the current timestamp from `window.performance.now`. Calls `TimeStep.stepLimitFPS` if an FPS limit is active, otherwise calls `TimeStep.step`.

name: Phaser.DOM.RequestAnimationFrame
doc: Abstracts away the use of `requestAnimationFrame` or `setTimeout` for the core game update loop, providing a unified interface regardless of which mechanism is in use. When `requestAnimationFrame` is available and not overridden, it is used to drive the game loop, which ties updates to the display refresh rate and pauses automatically when the tab is hidden.

name: Phaser.Events.EventEmitter

Every Scene has an instance of this class available via `scene.events`, and many Phaser objects extend or embed it to dispatch and receive events.

doc: DOM Element Game Objects are a way to control and manipulate HTML Elements over the top of your game. doc: Move the start of the gradient. You can animate gradients in this way.

doc: The repeat mode of the gradient. Gradient progress is evaluated as a number, where 0 is the start of the `shape` vector and 1 is the end.

doc: The shape mode of the gradient. Shapes are based on the `shape` vector.

doc: The start location of the gradient within its quad. The gradient emanates from this point.

doc: The shape vector of the gradient within its quad. This points from the start in the direction that the gradient flows.

doc: The filter lists for this Game Object. This is an object with `internal` and `external` properties.

doc: Whether any filters should be rendered on this Game Object. This is `true` by default, even if there are no filters yet.

doc: The maximum size of the base filter texture. Filters may use a larger texture after the base texture is rendered.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Gradient.filtersFocusContext
doc: Whether the filters should focus on the context, rather than attempt to focus on the Game Object. This is enabled automatically when enabling filters on objects which don't have well-defined bounds.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Gradient.filtersForceComposite
doc: Whether the Filters component should always draw to a framebuffer, even if there are no active filters.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.maxParticles
doc: Set to hard limit the amount of particle objects this emitter is allowed to create in total. This is the number of `Particle` instances it can create, not the number of 'alive' particles.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.maxAliveParticles
doc: The maximum number of alive and rendering particles this emitter will update. When this limit is reached, a particle needs to die before another can be emitted.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.stopAfter
doc: If set, either via the Emitter config, or by directly setting this property, the Particle Emitter will stop emitting particles once this total has been reached. It will then enter a 'stopped' state, firing the `STOP` event.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.duration
doc: The number of milliseconds this emitter will emit particles for when in flow mode, before it stops emission. A value of 0 (the default) means there is no duration.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.frequency
doc: For a flow emitter, the time interval (>= 0) between particle flow cycles in ms. A value of 0 means there is one particle flow cycle for each logic update (the maximum flow frequency).

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.emitting
doc: Controls if the emitter is currently emitting a particle flow (when frequency >= 0). Already alive particles will continue to update until they expire.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.particleBringToTop
doc: Newly emitted particles are added to the top of the particle list, i.e. rendered above those already alive.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.timeScale
doc: The time rate applied to active particles, affecting lifespan, movement, and tweens. Values larger than 1 are faster than normal.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.emitZones
doc: An array containing Particle Emission Zones. These can be either EdgeZones or RandomZones.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.deathZones
doc: An array containing Particle Death Zone objects. A particle is immediately killed as soon as its x/y coordinates intersect with any of the configured Death Zones.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.viewBounds
doc: An optional Rectangle object that is used during rendering to cull Particles from display. For example, if your particles are limited to only move within a 300x300 sized area from their origin, then you can set this Rectangle to those dimensions.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.follow
doc: A Game Object whose position is used as the particle origin.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.followOffset
doc: The offset of the particle origin from the {@link Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter#follow} target.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.trackVisible
doc: Whether the emitter's {@link Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter#visible} state will track the {@link Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter#follow} target's visibility state.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.frames
doc: The texture frames assigned to particles.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.randomFrame
doc: Whether texture {@link Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter#frames} are selected at random.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.frameQuantity
doc: The number of consecutive particles that receive a single texture frame (per frame cycle).

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.anims
doc: The animations assigned to particles.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.randomAnim
doc: Whether animations {@link Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter#anims} are selected at random.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.animQuantity
doc: The number of consecutive particles that receive a single animation (per frame cycle).

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.skipping
doc: An internal property used to tell when the emitter is in fast-forward mode.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.worldMatrix
doc: An internal Transform Matrix used to cache this emitters world matrix.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.sortProperty
doc: Optionally sort the particles before they render based on this property. The property must exist on the `Particle` class, such as `y`, `lifeT`, `scaleX`, etc.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.sortOrderAsc
doc: When `sortProperty` is defined this controls the sorting order, either ascending or descending. Toggle to control the visual effect.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.sortCallback
doc: The callback used to sort the particles. Only used if `sortProperty` has been set.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.processors
doc: A list of Particle Processors being managed by this Emitter.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.tintMode
doc: The tint mode used by the Particles in this Emitter. Available modes are: - Phaser.TintModes.MULTIPLY (default) - Phaser.TintModes.FILL - Phaser.TintModes.ADD - Phaser.TintModes.SCREEN - Phaser.TintModes.OVERLAY - Phaser.TintModes.HARD_LIGHT

doc: Called when this Game Object is added to a Scene. Registers this emitter with the Scene's update list so it receives `preUpdate` calls each frame.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.removedFromScene
doc: Called when this Game Object is removed from a Scene. Unregisters this emitter from the Scene's update list so it no longer receives `preUpdate` calls.

doc: The horizontal acceleration applied to emitted particles, in pixels per second squared. Accessing this property should typically return a number.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.accelerationY
doc: The vertical acceleration applied to emitted particles, in pixels per second squared. Accessing this property should typically return a number.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.maxVelocityX
doc: The maximum horizontal velocity emitted particles can reach, in pixels per second. Accessing this property should typically return a number.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.maxVelocityY
doc: The maximum vertical velocity emitted particles can reach, in pixels per second. Accessing this property should typically return a number.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.speed
doc: The initial speed of emitted particles, in pixels per second. If using this as a getter it will return the `speedX` value.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.speedX
doc: The initial horizontal speed of emitted particles, in pixels per second. Accessing this property should typically return a number.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.speedY

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.moveToY
doc: The y coordinate emitted particles move toward, when {@link Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter#moveTo} is true. Accessing this property should typically return a number.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.bounce
doc: The amount of velocity particles will use when rebounding off the emitter bounds, if set. A value of 0 means no bounce.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.particleScaleX
doc: The horizontal scale of emitted particles. This is relative to the Emitters scale and that of any parent.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.particleScaleY
doc: The vertical scale of emitted particles. This is relative to the Emitters scale and that of any parent.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.particleColor
doc: A color tint value that is applied to the texture of the emitted particle. The value should be given in hex format, i.e.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.colorEase
doc: Controls the easing function used when you have created an Emitter that uses the `color` property to interpolate the tint of Particles over their lifetime. Setting this has no effect if you haven't also applied a `particleColor` to this Emitter.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.particleTint
doc: A color tint value that is applied to the texture of the emitted particle. The value should be given in hex format, i.e.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.particleAlpha
doc: The alpha value of the emitted particles. This is a value between 0 and 1.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.lifespan
doc: The lifespan of the emitted particles. This value is given in milliseconds and defaults to 1000ms (1 second).

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.particleAngle
doc: The angle at which the particles are emitted. The values are given in degrees.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.particleRotate
doc: The rotation (or angle) of each particle when it is emitted. The value is given in degrees and uses a right-handed coordinate system, where 0 degrees points to the right, 90 degrees points down and -90 degrees points up.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.quantity
doc: The number of particles that are emitted each time an emission occurs, i.e. from one 'explosion' or each frame in a 'flow' cycle.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.delay
doc: The number of milliseconds to wait after emission before the particles start updating. This allows you to emit particles that appear 'static' or still on-screen and then, after this value, begin to move.

name: Phaser.GameObjects.Particles.ParticleEmitter.hold
doc: The number of milliseconds to wait after a particle has finished its life before it will be removed. This allows you to 'hold' a particle on the screen once it has reached its final state before it then vanishes.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.upElement
doc: The DOM element the Pointer was released on, taken from the DOM event. In a default set-up this will be the Canvas that Phaser is rendering to, or the Window element.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.camera
doc: The camera the Pointer interacted with during its last update. A Pointer can only ever interact with one camera at once, which will be the top-most camera in the list should multiple cameras be positioned on-top of each other.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.button
doc: A read-only property that indicates which button was pressed, or released, on the pointer during the most recent event. It is only set during `up` and `down` events.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.buttons
doc: A bitmask representing which mouse buttons are currently held down. The possible values are: 0: No button or un-initialized 1: Left button 2: Right button 4: Wheel button or middle button 8: 4th button (typically the "Browser Back" button) 16: 5th button (typically the "Browser Forward" button) For a mouse configured for left-handed use, the button actions are reversed.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.position
doc: The position of the Pointer in screen space.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.prevPosition
doc: The previous position of the Pointer in screen space. The old x and y values are stored in here during the InputManager.transformPointer call.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.velocity
doc: The current velocity of the Pointer, based on its current and previous positions. This value is smoothed out each frame, according to the `motionFactor` property.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.angle
doc: The current angle the Pointer is moving, in radians, based on its previous and current position. The angle is based on the old position facing to the current position.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.distance
doc: The distance the Pointer has moved, based on its previous and current position. This value is smoothed out each frame, according to the `motionFactor` property.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.smoothFactor
doc: The smoothing factor to apply to the Pointer position. Due to their nature, pointer positions are inherently noisy.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.motionFactor
doc: The factor applied to the motion smoothing each frame. This value is passed to the Smooth Step Interpolation that is used to calculate the velocity, angle and distance of the Pointer.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.worldX
doc: The x position of this Pointer, translated into the coordinate space of the most recent Camera it interacted with. If you wish to use this value _outside_ of an input event handler then you should update it first by calling the `Pointer.updateWorldPoint` method.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.worldY
doc: The y position of this Pointer, translated into the coordinate space of the most recent Camera it interacted with. If you wish to use this value _outside_ of an input event handler then you should update it first by calling the `Pointer.updateWorldPoint` method.

doc: Time when this Pointer was most recently moved (regardless of the state of its buttons, if any).

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.downY

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.upY

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.upTime

doc: Is the primary button down? (usually button 0, the left mouse button)

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.isDown

doc:
If the Pointer has a button pressed down at the time this method is called, it will return the distance between the Pointer's `downX` and `downY` values and the current position. If no button is held down, it will return the last recorded distance, based on where the Pointer was when the button was released.
@returns The distance the Pointer moved.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.getDistanceX
doc:
If the Pointer has a button pressed down at the time this method is called, it will return the horizontal distance between the Pointer's `downX` value and the current `x` position. If no button is held down, it will return the last recorded horizontal distance, based on where the Pointer was when the button was released.undefined
@returns The horizontal distance the Pointer moved.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.getDistanceY

If no button is held down, it will return the last recorded vertical distance, based on where the Pointer was when the button was released.undefined
@returns The vertical distance the Pointer moved.

name: Phaser.Input.Pointer.getDuration

@returns The duration the Pointer was held down for in milliseconds.

If no button is held down, it will return the last recorded angle, based on where the Pointer was when the button was released.
@returns The angle between the Pointer's coordinates in radians.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.threshold
doc: The Threshold filter which cuts off darker light from the image.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.blur
doc: The Blur filter which spreads out bright light from the image.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.radius
doc: The width of the shine, as a proportion of the size of the target.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.direction
doc: The direction the shine travels in. 0 is to the right, increasing clockwise.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.scale
doc: The length the shine travels, as a proportion of the size of the target. This is the length of the gradient shape vector.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.width
doc: The width of the gradient texture. By default, this is derived from the target.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.height
doc: The height of the gradient texture. By default, this is derived from the target.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.bands
doc: Custom color bands to use in the gradient. If this is defined, `shineColor` does nothing.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.colorFactor
doc: The factor which multiplies the shiny part of the image. Must be 4 numbers (RGBA).

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.displacementMap
doc: A displacement map to apply to the gradient. If not defined, no displacement is applied.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.displacement
doc: If a displacement map is applied, this is its strength.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.duration
doc: Duration of the shine animation (via the tween), in milliseconds.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.repeatDelay
doc: Delay between repetitions of the shine animation.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.ease
doc: Ease mode for the tween.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.yoyo
doc: Whether to move the shine back and forth. If not set, the shine constantly crosses the image in the same direction every time.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.useExternal
doc: Whether to add the shine effect in external space, where it relates to the screen. By default, it is in internal space, where it relates to the target.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.reveal
doc: Whether to use reveal mode. In reveal mode, the effect only shows the shiny part of the image; the rest is hidden.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.item
doc: The object or camera to which the shine is applied.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.gradient
doc: The gradient which controls the shine area. This is not added to the scene, so it will be garbage collected once all references and the tween are destroyed.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.dynamicTexture
doc: The texture where the gradient is rendered, after any filters are applied. This will be destroyed when the target is destroyed.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.tween
doc: The tween which controls the gradient motion. When this updates, the dynamicTexture is redrawn.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.parallelFilters
doc: The ParallelFilters filter which adds the shine to the image. This will not be defined if the Shine is in `reveal` mode.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.blendFilter
doc: The Blend filter which makes the image shine by multiplying it by the gradient. This controls the brightness of the shine.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.invert

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.blurRadius

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.blurSteps
doc: The number of steps to run blur on the mask. This value should always be an integer.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.blurQuality

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.scaleMode
doc: The scale mode to use when fitting the shape. 0 sets each axis to fill the region independently.

name: Phaser.Types.Actions.padding

doc: The background colors of the banner.

doc: A function to run at the start of the boot sequence.

doc: A function to run at the end of the boot sequence. At this point, all the game systems have started and plugins have been loaded.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.createContainer
doc: Should the game create a div element to act as a DOM Container? Only enable if you're using DOM Element objects. You must provide a parent object if you use this feature.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.behindCanvas
doc: Should the DOM Container that is created (if `dom.createContainer` is true) be positioned behind (true) or over the top (false, the default) of the game canvas?

name: Phaser.Types.Core.pointerEvents
doc: The default `pointerEvents` attribute set on the DOM Container.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.min
doc: The minimum acceptable rendering rate, in frames per second.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.target
doc: The optimum rendering rate, in frames per second. This does not enforce the fps rate, it merely tells Phaser what rate is considered optimal for this game.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.limit
doc: Enforces an fps rate limit that the game step will run at, regardless of browser frequency. 0 means 'no limit'.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.forceSetTimeOut
doc: Use setTimeout instead of requestAnimationFrame to run the game loop.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.deltaHistory
doc: Calculate the average frame delta from this many consecutive frame intervals.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.panicMax
doc: The amount of frames the time step counts before we trust the delta values again.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.smoothStep
doc: Apply delta smoothing during the game update to help avoid spikes?

name: Phaser.Types.Core.width
doc: The width of the game, in game pixels.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.height
doc: The height of the game, in game pixels.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.zoom
doc: Simple scale applied to the game canvas. 2 is double size, 0.5 is half size, etc.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.type
doc: Which renderer to use. Phaser.AUTO, Phaser.CANVAS, Phaser.HEADLESS, or Phaser.WEBGL.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.stableSort
doc: `true` or `1` = Use the built-in StableSort (needed for older browsers), `false` or `0` = Rely on ES2019 Array.sort being stable (modern browsers only), or `-1` = Try and determine this automatically based on browser inspection (not guaranteed to work, errs on side of caution).

name: Phaser.Types.Core.parent
doc: The DOM element that will contain the game canvas, or its `id`. If undefined, or if the named element doesn't exist, the game canvas is appended to the document body.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.canvas
doc: Provide your own Canvas element for Phaser to use instead of creating one.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.canvasStyle
doc: CSS styles to apply to the game canvas instead of Phasers default styles.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.customEnvironment
doc: Is Phaser running under a custom (non-native web) environment? If so, set this to `true` to skip internal Feature detection. If `true` the `renderType` cannot be left as `AUTO`.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.context
doc: Provide your own Canvas Context for Phaser to use, instead of creating one.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.scene
doc: A scene or scenes to add to the game. If several are given, the first is started; the remainder are started only if they have `{ active: true }`.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.seed
doc: Seed for the random number generator.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.title
doc: The title of the game. Shown in the browser console.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.url
doc: The URL of the game. Shown in the browser console.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.version
doc: The version of the game. Shown in the browser console.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.autoFocus
doc: Automatically call window.focus() when the game boots. Usually necessary to capture input events if the game is in a separate frame.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.input
doc: Input configuration, or `false` to disable all game input.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.disableContextMenu
doc: Disable the browser's default 'contextmenu' event (usually triggered by a right-button mouse click).

name: Phaser.Types.Core.banner
doc: Configuration for the banner printed in the browser console when the game starts.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.dom
doc: The DOM Container configuration object.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.fps
doc: Game loop configuration.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.render
doc: Game renderer configuration.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.callbacks
doc: Optional callbacks to run before or after game boot.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.images
doc: Images configuration.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.physics
doc: Physics configuration.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.plugins
doc: Plugins to install.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.scale
doc: The Scale Manager configuration.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.audio
doc: The Audio Configuration object.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.backgroundColor
doc: The background color of the game canvas. The default is black.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.antialias
doc: When set to `true`, WebGL uses linear interpolation to draw scaled or rotated textures, giving a smooth appearance. When set to `false`, WebGL uses nearest-neighbor interpolation, giving a crisper appearance.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.antialiasGL
doc: Sets the `antialias` property when the WebGL context is created. Setting this value does not impact any subsequent textures that are created, or the canvas style attributes.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.desynchronized
doc: When set to `true` it will create a desynchronized context for both 2D and WebGL. See https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2019/05/desynchronized for details.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.pixelArt
doc: Sets `antialias` to false and `roundPixels` to true. This is the best setting for pixel-art games.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.smoothPixelArt
doc: WebGL only. Sets `antialias` to true and `pixelArt` to false.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.roundPixels
doc: Draw texture-based Game Objects at only whole-integer positions. Game Objects without textures, like Graphics, ignore this property.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.selfShadow
doc: On textured objects with lighting, this enables self-shadowing based on the diffuse map.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.pathDetailThreshold
doc: Threshold for combining points into a single path in the WebGL renderer for Graphics objects. This can be overridden at the Graphics object level.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.transparent
doc: Whether the game canvas will be transparent. Boolean that indicates if the canvas contains an alpha channel.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.clearBeforeRender
doc: Whether the game canvas will be cleared between each rendering frame.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.preserveDrawingBuffer
doc: If the value is true the WebGL buffers will not be cleared and will preserve their values until cleared or overwritten by the author.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.premultipliedAlpha
doc: In WebGL mode, the drawing buffer contains colors with pre-multiplied alpha.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat
doc: Let the browser abort creating a WebGL context if it judges performance would be unacceptable.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.powerPreference
doc: "high-performance", "low-power" or "default". A hint to the browser on how much device power the game might use.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.batchSize
doc: The default WebGL batch size. Represents the number of _quads_ that can be added to a single batch.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.maxLights
doc: The maximum number of lights allowed to be visible within range of a single Camera in the LightManager.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.maxTextures
doc: When in WebGL mode, this sets the maximum number of GPU Textures to use. The default, -1, will use all available units.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.mipmapFilter
doc: The mipmap magFilter to be used when creating WebGL textures.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.mipmapRegeneration
doc: Whether to regenerate mipmaps for framebuffers.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.autoMobileTextures
doc: If iOS or Android detected, automatically restrict WebGL to use 1 texture per batch. This can help performance on some devices.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.expandParent
doc: Is the Scale Manager allowed to adjust the CSS height property of the parent and/or document body to be 100%?

name: Phaser.Types.Core.mode

name: Phaser.Types.Core.min

name: Phaser.Types.Core.max
doc: The maximum width the canvas can be scaled up to.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.autoRound

name: Phaser.Types.Core.autoCenter

name: Phaser.Types.Core.resizeInterval
doc: How many ms should elapse before checking if the browser size has changed?

name: Phaser.Types.Core.fullscreenTarget

name: Phaser.Types.Core.target

name: Phaser.Types.Core.default

name: Phaser.Types.Core.missing

name: Phaser.Types.Core.white
doc: A base64 encoded image file to use as the 'white' texture.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.mouse

name: Phaser.Types.Core.touch

name: Phaser.Types.Core.gamepad

name: Phaser.Types.Core.activePointers

name: Phaser.Types.Core.smoothFactor
doc: The smoothing factor to apply during Pointer movement. See {@link Phaser.Input.Pointer#smoothFactor}.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.windowEvents

name: Phaser.Types.Core.target

name: Phaser.Types.Core.capture
doc: `preventDefault` will be called on every non-modified key which has a key code in this array. By default it is empty.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.baseURL
doc: A URL used to resolve paths given to the loader. Example: 'http://labs.phaser.io/assets/'.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.path
doc: A URL path used to resolve relative paths given to the loader. Example: 'images/sprites/'.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.maxParallelDownloads
doc: The maximum number of resources the loader will start loading at once.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.crossOrigin
doc: 'anonymous', 'use-credentials', or `undefined`. If you're not making cross-origin requests, leave this as `undefined`.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.responseType
doc: The response type of the XHR request, e.g. `blob`, `text`, etc.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.async
doc: Should the XHR request use async or not?

name: Phaser.Types.Core.user
doc: Optional username for all XHR requests.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.password
doc: Optional password for all XHR requests.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.timeout
doc: Optional XHR timeout value, in ms.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.localScheme

name: Phaser.Types.Core.withCredentials
doc: Optional XHR withCredentials value.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.imageLoadType
doc: Optional load type for image, `XHR` is default, or `HTMLImageElement` for a lightweight way.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.maxRetries

name: Phaser.Types.Core.target

name: Phaser.Types.Core.preventDefaultUp
doc: If `true` the DOM `mouseup` event will have `preventDefault` set.

name: Phaser.Types.Core.preventDefaultMove

name: Phaser.Types.Core.preventDefaultWheel

name: Phaser.Types.Core.arcade

name: Phaser.Types.Core.start

name: Phaser.Types.Filters.rotationSource

name: Phaser.Types.Filters.facingPower

name: Phaser.Types.Filters.outputRatio

name: Phaser.Types.Filters.samplesX

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Image
sig: class Image extends Phaser.GameObjects.Image implements Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Components.Acceleration, Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Components.Angular, Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Components.Bounce, Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Components.Collision, Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Components.Debug, Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Components.Drag, Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Components.Enable, Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Components.Friction, Phaser.
doc: An Arcade Physics Image is a standard Image Game Object with an Arcade Physics body and related physics components mixed in. It is the lightest-weight physics-enabled Game Object available in Arcade Physics, making it ideal for static scenery, collectibles, platforms, bullets, or any non-animated object that needs to participate in physics collisions and overlap checks.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.world
doc: The Arcade Physics simulation this Body belongs to.

doc: The Game Object this Body belongs to. As of Phaser 3.60 this is now optional and can be undefined.

doc: The color of this Body on the debug display.

doc: Whether this Body is updated by the physics simulation.

doc: Whether this Body is circular (true) or rectangular (false).

doc: If this Body is circular, this is the unscaled radius of the Body, as set by setCircle(), in source pixels. The true radius is equal to `halfWidth`.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.offset
doc: The offset of this Body's position from its Game Object's position, in source pixels.

doc: This body's rotation, in degrees, based on its angular acceleration and angular velocity. The Body's rotation controls the `angle` of its Game Object.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.preRotation
doc: The Body rotation, in degrees, during the previous step.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.width
doc: The width of the Body, in pixels. If the Body is circular, this is also the diameter.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.height
doc: The height of the Body, in pixels. If the Body is circular, this is also the diameter.

doc: The unscaled width of the Body, in source pixels, as set by setSize(). The default is the width of the Body's Game Object's texture frame.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.sourceHeight
doc: The unscaled height of the Body, in source pixels, as set by setSize(). The default is the height of the Body's Game Object's texture frame.

doc: Half the Body's width, in pixels.

doc: The center of the Body. The midpoint of its `position` (top-left corner) and its bottom-right corner.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.velocity
doc: The Body's velocity, in pixels per second.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.newVelocity
doc: The Body's change in position (due to velocity) at the last step, in pixels. The size of this value depends on the simulation's step rate.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.deltaMax
doc: The Body's absolute maximum change in position, in pixels per step.
