doc: The Body's change in velocity, in pixels per second squared.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.allowDrag
doc: Whether this Body's velocity is affected by its `drag`.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.drag
doc: When `useDamping` is false (the default), this is absolute loss of velocity due to movement, in pixels per second squared. When `useDamping` is true, this is a damping multiplier between 0 and 1.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.allowGravity
doc: Whether this Body's position is affected by gravity (local or world).

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.gravity
doc: Acceleration due to gravity (specific to this Body), in pixels per second squared. Total gravity is the sum of this vector and the simulation's `gravity`.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.bounce
doc: Rebound following a collision, relative to 1.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.worldBounce
doc: Rebound following a collision with the world boundary, relative to 1. If null, `bounce` is used instead.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.customBoundsRectangle
doc: The rectangle used for world boundary collisions. By default it is set to the world boundary rectangle.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.onWorldBounds
doc: Whether the simulation emits a `worldbounds` event when this Body collides with the world boundary (and `collideWorldBounds` is also true).

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.onCollide
doc: Whether the simulation emits a `collide` event when this Body collides with another.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.onOverlap
doc: Whether the simulation emits an `overlap` event when this Body overlaps with another.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.maxVelocity
doc: The absolute maximum velocity of this body, in pixels per second. The horizontal and vertical components are applied separately.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.maxSpeed
doc: The maximum speed this Body is allowed to reach, in pixels per second. If not negative it limits the scalar value of speed.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.friction
doc: If this Body is `immovable` and in motion, `friction` is the proportion of this Body's motion received by the riding Body on each axis, relative to 1. The horizontal component (x) is applied only when two colliding Bodies are separated vertically.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.useDamping
doc: If this Body is using `drag` for deceleration this property controls how the drag is applied. If set to `true` drag will use a damping effect rather than a linear approach.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.angularVelocity
doc: The rate of change of this Body's `rotation`, in degrees per second.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.angularAcceleration
doc: The Body's angular acceleration (change in angular velocity), in degrees per second squared.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.angularDrag
doc: Loss of angular velocity due to angular movement, in degrees per second. Angular drag is applied only when angular acceleration is zero.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.maxAngular
doc: The Body's maximum angular velocity, in degrees per second.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.mass
doc: The Body's inertia, relative to a default unit (1). With `bounce`, this affects the exchange of momentum (velocities) during collisions.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.angle
doc: The calculated angle of this Body's velocity vector, in radians, during the last step.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.speed
doc: The calculated magnitude of the Body's velocity, in pixels per second, during the last step.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.facing
doc: The direction of the Body's velocity, as calculated during the last step. This is a numeric constant value (FACING_UP, FACING_DOWN, FACING_LEFT, FACING_RIGHT).

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.immovable
doc: Whether this Body can be moved by collisions with another Body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.pushable
doc: Sets if this Body can be pushed by another Body. A body that cannot be pushed will reflect back all of the velocity it is given to the colliding body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.slideFactor
doc: The Slide Factor of this Body. The Slide Factor controls how much velocity is preserved when this Body is pushed by another Body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.moves
doc: Whether the Body's position and rotation are affected by its velocity, acceleration, drag, and gravity.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.customSeparateX
doc: A flag disabling the default horizontal separation of colliding bodies. Pass your own `collideCallback` to the collider.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.customSeparateY
doc: A flag disabling the default vertical separation of colliding bodies. Pass your own `collideCallback` to the collider.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.overlapX
doc: The amount of horizontal overlap (before separation), if this Body is colliding with another.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.overlapY
doc: The amount of vertical overlap (before separation), if this Body is colliding with another.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.overlapR
doc: The amount of overlap (before separation), if this Body is circular and colliding with another circular body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.embedded
doc: Whether this Body is overlapped with another and both are not moving, on at least one axis.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.collideWorldBounds
doc: Whether this Body interacts with the world boundary.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.checkCollision
doc: Whether this Body is checked for collisions and for which directions. You can set `checkCollision.none = true` to disable collision checks.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.touching
doc: Whether this Body is colliding with a Body or Static Body and in which direction. In a collision where both bodies have zero velocity, `embedded` will be set instead.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.wasTouching
doc: This Body's `touching` value during the previous step.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.blocked
doc: Whether this Body is colliding with a Static Body, a tile, or the world boundary. In a collision with a Static Body, if this Body has zero velocity then `embedded` will be set instead.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.syncBounds
doc: Whether to automatically synchronize this Body's dimensions to the dimensions of its Game Object's visual bounds.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.physicsType
doc: The Body's physics type (dynamic or static).

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.collisionCategory
doc: The Arcade Physics Body Collision Category. This can be set to any valid collision bitfield value.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.collisionMask
doc: The Arcade Physics Body Collision Mask. See the `setCollidesWith` method for more details.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.directControl
doc: Is this Body under direct control, outside of the physics engine? For example, are you trying to move it via a Tween? Or have it follow a path? If so then you can enable this boolean so that the Body will calculate its velocity based purely on its change in position each frame. This allows you to then tween the position and still have it collide with other objects.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.updateBounds
doc: Updates the Body's `transform`, `width`, `height`, and `center` from its Game Object. The Body's `position` isn't changed.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.updateCenter
doc: Updates the Body's `center` from its `position`, `width`, and `height`.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.Body.updateFromGameObject
doc: Updates the Body's `position`, `width`, `height`, and `center` from its Game Object and `offset`. You don't need to call this for Dynamic Bodies, as it happens automatically during the physics step.

@param clear Set the `wasTouching` values to their defaults. Default false.

doc: The Arcade Physics simulation this Static Body belongs to.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.gameObject
doc: The Game Object this Static Body belongs to. As of Phaser 3.60 this is now optional and can be undefined.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.isBody
doc: A quick-test flag that signifies this is a Body, used in the World collision handler.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.debugShowBody
doc: Whether the Static Body's boundary is drawn to the debug display.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.debugBodyColor
doc: The color of this Static Body on the debug display.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.enable
doc: Whether this Static Body is updated by the physics simulation.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.isCircle
doc: Whether this Static Body's boundary is circular (`true`) or rectangular (`false`).

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.radius
doc: If this Static Body is circular, this is the radius of the boundary, as set by {@link Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody#setCircle}, in pixels. Equal to `halfWidth`.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.offset
doc: The offset set by {@link Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody#setCircle} or {@link Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody#setSize}. This doesn't affect the Static Body's position, because a Static Body does not follow its Game Object.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.position
doc: The position of this Static Body within the simulation.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.width
doc: The width of the Static Body's boundary, in pixels. If the Static Body is circular, this is also the Static Body's diameter.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.height
doc: The height of the Static Body's boundary, in pixels. If the Static Body is circular, this is also the Static Body's diameter.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.halfWidth
doc: Half the Static Body's width, in pixels. If the Static Body is circular, this is also the Static Body's radius.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.halfHeight
doc: Half the Static Body's height, in pixels. If the Static Body is circular, this is also the Static Body's radius.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.center
doc: The center of the Static Body's boundary. This is the midpoint of its `position` (top-left corner) and its bottom-right corner.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.velocity
doc: A constant zero velocity used by the Arcade Physics simulation for calculations.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.allowGravity
doc: A constant `false` value expected by the Arcade Physics simulation.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.gravity
doc: Gravitational force applied specifically to this Body. Values are in pixels per second squared.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.bounce
doc: Rebound, or restitution, following a collision, relative to 1. Always zero for a Static Body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.onWorldBounds
doc: Whether the simulation emits a `worldbounds` event when this StaticBody collides with the world boundary. Always false for a Static Body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.onCollide
doc: Whether the simulation emits a `collide` event when this StaticBody collides with another.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.onOverlap
doc: Whether the simulation emits an `overlap` event when this StaticBody overlaps with another.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.mass
doc: The StaticBody's inertia, relative to a default unit (1). With `bounce`, this affects the exchange of momentum (velocities) during collisions.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.immovable
doc: Whether this object can be moved by collisions with another body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.pushable
doc: Sets if this Body can be pushed by another Body. A body that cannot be pushed will reflect back all of the velocity it is given to the colliding body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.customSeparateX
doc: A flag disabling the default horizontal separation of colliding bodies. Pass your own `collideHandler` to the collider.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.customSeparateY
doc: A flag disabling the default vertical separation of colliding bodies. Pass your own `collideHandler` to the collider.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.overlapX
doc: The amount of horizontal overlap (before separation), if this Body is colliding with another.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.overlapY
doc: The amount of vertical overlap (before separation), if this Body is colliding with another.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.overlapR
doc: The amount of overlap (before separation), if this StaticBody is circular and colliding with another circular body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.embedded
doc: Whether this StaticBody has ever overlapped with another while both were not moving.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.collideWorldBounds
doc: Whether this StaticBody interacts with the world boundary. Always false for a Static Body.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.checkCollision
doc: Whether this StaticBody is checked for collisions and for which directions. You can set `checkCollision.none = true` to disable collision checks.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.touching
doc: This property is kept for compatibility with Dynamic Bodies. Avoid using it.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.wasTouching
doc: This property is kept for compatibility with Dynamic Bodies. Avoid using it.

name: Phaser.Physics.Arcade.StaticBody.blocked

doc: Always separate overlapping Bodies horizontally before vertically. False (the default) means Bodies are first separated on the axis of greater gravity, or the vertical axis if neither is greater.

However, at certain limits, the cost of clearing and inserting the bodies into the tree every frame becomes more expensive than the search speed gains it provides.

name: Phaser.Textures.TextureSource
doc: A Texture Source is the encapsulation of the actual source data for a Texture. It wraps the raw pixel data — typically an Image Element loaded from the file system or network, a Canvas Element, or a Video Element — and manages the corresponding WebGL texture object used by the renderer.

doc: The source of the image data. This is either an Image Element, a Canvas Element, a Video Element, a RenderTexture or a WebGLTextureWrapper.

doc: The image data. This is either an Image element, Canvas element, Video Element, or null if the `source` is not an HTMLElement.

name: Phaser.Textures.TextureSource.height

name: Phaser.Time.Clock
doc: The Clock is a Scene plugin that manages time and schedules Timer Events for its parent Scene. You can use it to run callbacks after a delay, on a repeating interval, or in a loop, all governed by the Scene's time rather than the system clock.

name: Phaser.Time.Clock.startTime
doc: The time the Clock (and Scene) started, in milliseconds. This can be compared to the `time` parameter passed to a Scene's `update` method.

name: Phaser.Time.Clock.timeScale
doc: The scale of the Clock's time delta. The time delta is the time elapsed between two consecutive frames and influences the speed of time for this Clock and anything which uses it, such as its Timer Events.

name: Phaser.Time.Clock.paused

Schedules all active Timer Events for removal at the start of the frame.undefined

name: Phaser.Time.Clock.preUpdate
doc: Updates the arrays of active and pending Timer Events. Called at the start of the frame.

Phaser.Time.Timeline
doc: A Timeline is a way to schedule events to happen at specific times in the future. You can think of it as an event sequencer for your game, allowing you to schedule the running of callbacks, events and other actions at specific times in the future.

name: Phaser.Time.Timeline.totalComplete

name: Phaser.Time.Timeline.loop
doc: The number of times this timeline should loop. If this value is -1 or any negative number, this Timeline will loop indefinitely.

name: Phaser.Time.Timeline.iteration
doc: The number of times this Timeline has looped. This value is incremented each loop if looping is enabled.

doc: An array of all the Timeline Events.

name: Phaser.Time.Timeline.preUpdate

Resumes this Timeline from a paused state. The Timeline will carry on from where it left off.

Stops this Timeline. This will set the `paused` and `complete` properties to `true`.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent
doc: A Timer Event represents a delayed function call. It's managed by a Scene's {@link Clock} and will call its function after a set amount of time has passed.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.constructor
doc: @param config The configuration for the Timer Event, including its delay and callback.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.delay
doc: The delay in ms at which this TimerEvent fires.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.repeat
doc: The total number of times this TimerEvent will repeat before finishing.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.repeatCount
doc: If repeating, this value contains the current countdown of how many repeats are still to come. It starts at the value of {@link #repeat} and counts down to zero each time the Timer Event fires.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.loop
doc: True if this TimerEvent loops, otherwise false.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.callback
doc: The callback that will be called when the TimerEvent occurs.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.callbackScope
doc: The scope in which the callback will be called.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.args
doc: Additional arguments to be passed to the callback.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.timeScale
doc: A time scale factor applied to the elapsed time used to update this Timer Event. Values greater than 1 will cause the event to fire sooner, while values less than 1 will delay it.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.startAt
doc: The number of milliseconds into the elapsed time to start the Timer Event from. This allows a long-duration repeating Timer Event to fire sooner on its first iteration without affecting the duration of subsequent repeats.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.elapsed
doc: The time in milliseconds which has elapsed since the Timer Event's creation. This value is local for the Timer Event and is relative to its Clock.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.paused
doc: Whether or not this timer is paused.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.hasDispatched
doc: Whether the Timer Event's function has been called. When the Timer Event fires, this property will be set to `true` before the callback function is invoked and will be reset immediately afterward if the Timer Event should repeat.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.reset
Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getProgress
doc:
Gets the progress of the current iteration, not factoring in repeats.undefined
@returns A number between 0 and 1 representing the current progress.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getOverallProgress
doc:
Gets the progress of the timer overall, factoring in repeats.undefined
@returns The overall progress of the Timer Event, between 0 and 1.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getRepeatCount
doc:
Returns the number of times this Timer Event will repeat before finishing. This should not be confused with the number of times the Timer Event will fire before finishing.
@returns How many times the Timer Event will repeat.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getElapsed
doc:
Returns the local elapsed time for the current iteration of the Timer Event.undefined
@returns The local elapsed time in milliseconds.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getElapsedSeconds
doc:
Returns the local elapsed time for the current iteration of the Timer Event in seconds.undefined
@returns The local elapsed time in seconds.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getRemaining
doc:
Returns the time interval until the next iteration of the Timer Event.undefined
@returns The time interval in milliseconds.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getRemainingSeconds
doc:
Returns the time interval until the next iteration of the Timer Event in seconds.undefined
@returns The time interval in seconds.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getOverallRemaining

Returns the time interval until the last iteration of the Timer Event.undefined
@returns The time interval in milliseconds.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.getOverallRemainingSeconds
doc:
Returns the time interval until the last iteration of the Timer Event in seconds.undefined
@returns The time interval in seconds.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.remove

Forces the Timer Event to immediately expire, thus scheduling its removal in the next frame.
@param dispatchCallback If `true`, the function of the Timer Event will be called before its removal. Default false.

name: Phaser.Time.TimerEvent.destroy
doc: Destroys all object references in the Timer Event, i.e. its callback, scope, and arguments.
